Kept so `npm run test:headhunter-completion-once` can rebuild the published node from archive + patch.
_why: exec 2024 posted SEVEN completion callbacks for one search and six carried wrong data: alternating "No candidates passed the preliminary AI score threshold (25)." and totalSent: 4, for a search that had actually delivered 13. Only the backend's idempotency guard saved the stored result, and only because the correct payload happened to arrive first.
_supersedes: An earlier draft of this patch guarded ONLY on `sd.hhCompleted[searchId]`, i.e. first-arrival-wins. That was WRONG: it reduced 7 callbacks to 1 without guaranteeing the 1 is correct, so it would have MOVED the ordering risk from the backend into n8n instead of removing it. If a spurious payload arrived first it would have been locked in and the correct one discarded. Rejected before publishing.

_rootCause.1_fanOut: `Stream Batch Done` has TWO inbound branches - `Has Match? [b1]` (rejected candidates) and `Accumulate Candidate [b0]` (accepted). A node with two inbound branches RUNS ONCE PER BRANCH, so every batch produces two independent batch-end signals. It is also `runOnceForEachItem`, so each run emits one item per candidate (13 for one batch in exec 2024).
_rootCause.2_repeatedDone: Those extra arrivals make `Split In Batches` fire its done branch repeatedly - 5 times in exec 2024.
_rootCause.3_destructiveFinalize: THE DECISIVE ONE. `Finalize Top N Send` and `Finalize Phase 2 Send` both delete `sd.hhCandidates[searchId]` and overwrite `hhPhase1SentCount` on their FIRST run, then return `__completeOnly: true` when the pool is empty. `Has Final Candidates?` routes `__completeOnly` straight to `Prepare Complete Search`. So each extra done produces a completion computed from state the first run already destroyed - which is why the payloads were WRONG, not merely duplicated.

_theTerminalSignal.insight: The workflow ALREADY computes a genuine terminal, in `Track Send Progress`: it emits `__completeSearch: true` only once `prog.sent >= prog.expected` for the final phase, and it carries the correct `phase1Count` / `totalSent`. `__completeOnly` is the ambiguous one - it means EITHER a search that truly had nothing to send, OR a repeat finalize run recomputing from destroyed state.
_theTerminalSignal.rule: Tell them apart with existing state, never with arrival order: if `sd.hhSendProgress[searchId]` shows anything was expected or sent, then an authoritative `__completeSearch` is the real completion and any `__completeOnly` is a repeat, so drop it. If nothing was ever sent (`expected` and `sent` both 0, or no progress record at all) then `__completeOnly` IS the only completion that will ever arrive, so let it through.
_theTerminalSignal.whyOrderIndependent: A spurious `__completeOnly` is dropped BEFORE it can set `hhCompleted`, so it cannot win a race no matter when it arrives. The `hhCompleted` flag then only ever guards genuine terminals.
_theTerminalSignal.failurePathPreserved: `All Serp Pages Failed? [b0]` also reaches `Prepare Complete Search` carrying `__completeOnly`, but on that path nothing was ever sent, so `hhSendProgress` is absent and the payload passes through unchanged.

_whyHere: The guard sits at `Prepare Complete Search` rather than at each source because there are THREE sources - `Has Final Candidates? [b1]`, `Complete Search Now? [b0]` and `All Serp Pages Failed? [b0]`. Guarding the single point where they converge covers all three in one edit.

_scope: One parameter on one node. No change to `Split In Batches` (the reset fix published as 191c06f9 is untouched), `Stream Batch Done`, either finalize node, any message text, query generation, `matchesPosition`, billing or EnrichLayer.
_knownLimits: This stops wrong and duplicate callbacks. It does NOT stop the extra done firings, and it does NOT stop the finalize nodes recomputing from destroyed state - it prevents those values reaching the backend. Making the finalize nodes idempotent, or storing the final counts once and reading them back, is a larger separate change.

`sd.hhCompleted` and `sd.hhSendProgress` are process-local workflow static data and are lost on an n8n restart, so a search spanning a restart could complete twice. The backend guard covers that residual case.

`return []` from a Code v2 node: `Track Send Progress` carries a comment saying n8n rejects empty output. Repro exec 2028 returned [] from a Code v2 node in the same `runOnceForAllItems` mode and the execution succeeded, so that comment appears to apply to `runOnceForEachItem` rather than this mode. Flagged rather than assumed; it is exercised by the repro on every guarded run.

Not yet observed in a real search. The next 20-tier search that triggers phase 2 is the live proof: expect exactly one `Complete Search` call, ok:true, zero idempotencyCollision, and the correct totalSent.
